title: Support WandBLogger in Fabric
body:
### Description & Motivation

Right now there are only the following loggers available in `lightning.fabric`:

- Logger
- CSVLogger
- TensorBoardLogger

I would like for there to be a `WandbLogger`, similar to that available for the regular `Trainer` interface.

### Alternatives

- It seems I cannot use the regular `WandbLogger`, as it needs to be passed to a `Trainer` object. 
- I tried to use `wandb` directly, but it seems to launch multiple runs for each ddp process.


cc @participant9 @participant2 @participant10 @participant11 @participant12 @participant13

comments.author: reporter
comments.body: Is there a reason why the regular loggers (https://lightning.ai/docs/pytorch/stable/api/lightning.pytorch.loggers.wandb.html#module-lightning.pytorch.loggers.wandb) are incompatible with `lightning.fabric`?

comments.author: participant1
comments.body:
HI @reporter ,

Given these limitations, it could be helpful to explore other options for implementing a WandbLogger in the lightning.fabric module. One approach could be to create a custom logger class that wraps around the regular WandbLogger and is specifically designed to work with the fabric module's distributed training setup.

This custom logger could handle the launching of the Weights & Biases run for each process in a DDP setup, ensuring that only one run is created per process. It could also provide additional functionality or customization options tailored specifically to the needs of users working with the fabric module.

comments.body:
A quick update is that I was able to actually pass the regular `WandbLogger` to the `fabric` module and it seems to be working. I think what happened was I saw an unrelated error, and noticed `WandbLogger` was not mentioned on the fabric loggers page, so I just assumed it was unsupported.

Out of curiosity why is there a separate loggers page for fabric if (presumably) the regular lightning loggers work? Would there be other problems I haven’t yet seen yet?

comments.author: participant1
comments.body:
Great to hear that you were able to use the regular WandbLogger with the fabric module!

 Regarding your question on the separate loggers page for Fabric, it's important to note that while Fabric is built on top of PyTorch Lightning, it has some unique features and requirements compared to a typical PyTorch Lightning project. 
This means that although most of the functionality of PyTorch Lightning should work seamlessly with Fabric, there may be cases where certain components need to be specifically designed or configured to work with Fabric. 

The Fabric documentation includes a list of supported loggers that have been tested and verified to work well with Fabric. These loggers have been specifically integrated with Fabric and provide additional functionality beyond what is available in the standard PyTorch Lightning loggers. However, this does not mean that other loggers won't work with Fabric, as you have demonstrated with the WandbLogger.

comments.author: participant2
comments.body:
Hi everyone, I can explain this. 

> Where does it say there are cases where certain components of the loggers "need to be specifically designed or configured to work with Fabric"?

It is not that the loggers need to be rewritten completely or anything like that. It is just that some loggers have trainer-specific hooks that wouldn't make sense in Fabric. If we just plugged the loggers as they are from PL into Fabric, it would work but then users could call APIs that would error out due to the missing code path into the Trainer. Another reason related to that is that we don't want a depencency from Fabric -> Trainer (the other way around would be ok). 

So the simple approach we take for the loggers is: 1) place their core implementation in `lightning.fabric.loggers` (no trainer assumptions). 2) Provide a second implementation in `lightning.pytorch.loggers` that reuses the code from Fabric but provides a superset of functionality with additional hooks etc. useful when used together with the Trainer. This is a relatively straightforward refactor. 

Let's keep the issue open. I am aware that we need to port the remaining loggers over, I just haven't had the time. Help from the community would be the best thing ever but I can also look into it in the next few days if it is difficult to do.

> It seems to work for me, but I noticed it's not actually part of the fabric submodule

Yes the basic functionality should work if you use the logger standalone. Feel free to continue doing that.

comments.author: participant8
comments.body:
Hey @participant4, thank you for your contribution.

We recently had internal discussions on the balance to strike between Fabric being batteries included vs keeping the core as lean as possible in the spirit of the library, and we opted for the second.

This is not to say that we are against such integrations. It only means that we would like to keep them out of core. We'll be happy to acknowledge the existence of an external package that provides this integration.

comments.author: participant4
comments.body:
Hey @participant8,

Thank you for the update and for considering the integration. I understand and respect the decision to maintain a lean core for Fabric in line with the library's philosophy.

In light of this, I'm exploring the possibility of moving the Fabric integration into an external package, possibly as part of the core`wandb` SDK or our additional package `wandb-addons`

However, I'm concerned about the discoverability of these integrations when they're not included in the core package. To help with this, could we consider adding a section in the Fabric documentation dedicated to third-party integrations? This could significantly enhance the visibility of external packages and provide users with easy access to additional functionality.

Thanks again for your consideration and support. I look forward to contributing further to the Lightning community.
